r0.why: Energy for muscle contraction, nerve impulses, chemical synthesis [1]; all known life and 'molecular unit of currency' for intracellular energy transfer [2].

r1.why: 'Besides carrying energy' relies on ATP's energy role, which is in uncited [1]; cited [5],[7],[9],[11] give only structure, labels and DNA/RNA precursor.

r2.why: ADP/AMP [3], triphosphate to di-/monophosphate with adenine and sugar unchanged [10], oxidative phosphorylation regenerates [4], repeated cycling in aerobic metabolism [28].

r3.why: ~50 kg (~100 mol) recycled daily by synthesis and hydrolysis [6]; ratio ten orders from equilibrium, ATP fivefold ADP [22].

r4.why: Polyanionic, high-affinity metal binding [12],[13]; mostly Mg complex on phosphate oxygens [16]; Mg strongly affects protein interaction [15]; pH 6.8-7.4 stability and rapid hydrolysis at extremes [20],[21].

r5.why: Three main eukaryotic pathways [29]; respiration = pathways 1+2, ~30 ATP per glucose [30]; mainly mitochondria, nearly 25% of cell volume, in non-photosynthetic aerobic eukaryotes [31].

r6.why: All steps match [32],[35]-[38],[40]-[45]: two phases of five steps, ATP invested at steps 1 and 3, 2 g3p to 2 pyruvate, 2 ATP at steps 7 and 10 from ADP, net 2, pyruvate feeds citric acid cycle making more ATP.
